sources.transitionableProps: A thin lath soaked through holds a bend as it dries in place, and is set in a couple of days (the Lac du Flambeau build, canoe.csumc.wisc.edu); in the bundle it dries as fast
sources.soaking: recipes/barrel/lath.json: water enters the same thin wood by the same diffusion it leaves by, so a lath soaks through in as long as it takes to dry; it takes up about a third of its dry weight, from air-dry past the fibre saturation point (Wood Handbook, FPL-GTR-282, ch. 4): 0.08 L a metre for a lath of 1 by 6 cm of white cedar, 400 kg/m³
sources.length: A lath is split from a pole as long as the row it came from; a place on a vessel takes any lath at least as long as it, cut down, the offcut lost
sources.split: recipes/grid/laths.json: a pole's billet, some 11 cm square, halved four times along its grain gives 16 laths of about 1 by 6 cm (Adney & Chapelle 1964: canoe ribs ⅜ by 2½ to 3 inches, sheathing thinner)
